# Backend merge validation (2026-11-04)

The NVIDIA/TLE foundation contains the shared language, analysis, call ABI,
pipe, communication-runtime and NVIDIA lowering changes. The AMD/RDNA and
Iluvatar extensions are separate branches based on that foundation. Their PRs
must be retargeted to main after the foundation merges. No independent MThreads
source change exists in this batch. Model code and model dependency changes
belong to a subsequent PR.

## Hierarchical device-mesh regression

Root cause: `python/triton/experimental/tle/language/distributed.py`,
`device_mesh.__init__`, `_collect_cluster_members_by_outer_coord`, and
`_infer_submesh_barrier_group`. Per-rank launch dimensions omit node/device
axes, while slicing retains physical IDs in the complete topology. Decoding
those IDs against launch_shape rejects valid IDs (15 and 96 in the existing
regressions) and confuses rank axes with CTA axes.

Preserve the original physical shape and names through slice/reshape views.
Decode membership in that domain, then project cluster axes into the per-rank
launch domain. Rank coordinates remain outer coordinates, so different masks
across ranks are still rejected. Device/world scope validation checks topology
axes rather than program_id dimensions. Mesh equality and hashing include the
physical domain to prevent distinct views from sharing JIT identities.

Reproducer (CPU only):

```sh
conda run -n flagtree pytest -q python/test/tle/unit/test_tle_distributed.py \
  -k infer_hierarchical_submesh
```

All three existing hierarchical-submesh tests fail with the pre-fix module
from commit 45e17f38 and pass with this change. Their expected cluster masks
are unchanged. The broader host suite also covers slicing, flatten/reshape,
rank and block axes, structural equality, and rejection of inconsistent masks.
The mesh change affects language-side topology analysis, shared by every
backend; it does not change a backend's barrier instruction implementation.

## Source-level validation

An isolated, normal CMake build of the NVIDIA/TLE closure built both the Python
compiler extension and triton-opt successfully. The complete TLE lit suite
passes 154/154 tests. The selected host/API/parser suite passes 95 tests with
7 CUDA-dependent skips and 3 subtests. All processes were waited for and their
actual exit codes recorded; these checks use the extension built from this
split, not a previously installed compiler extension.

The reader-contract diagnostic test originally ran both NVWS and RDNA passes.
The NVIDIA branch keeps its NVWS run; the AMD branch adds a separate RDNA run
with the same inputs and expected diagnostics. Neither backend's assertions
are removed.

On NVIDIA H800, the isolated extension also passes 57 GPU regression tests
covering bit-exact async-copy fills, cyclic and empty pipes of capacities
1/2/3/5, noinline producer/consumer calls, and masked/unmasked dynamic shared
scatter. Tests use the normal CUDA header/toolchain installation assets.

## Runtime prerequisites and remaining hardware coverage

The communication tests use the FlagCX SDK Python wrapper generated by the
normal SDK installation flow. Capacity discovery requires the SDK wrapper and
matching C ABI that expose supports_intra_barrier_count_query. The generated
wrapper and SDK libraries are external dependencies, not tracked in these PRs.
Host fixtures validate the capacity protocol; they do not establish distributed
hardware correctness. AMD and Iluvatar hardware execution must be performed
on their respective devices before those PRs become merge-ready.

Full-model performance from the model branch is not a validation result for
these independent compiler PRs. Each backend must retain its own correctness
and performance evidence.
